title: eval/rubric.json
description: The scoring surface, not a list of test names (DESIGN.md 10.2). eval.py runs every `automated` entry against the DEPLOYED agency, reading stored records rather than re-probing the world, and writes PRODUCT_EVAL.md. The kind split is the point: `automated` rows carry pass/fail and the evidence read; `evidence` rows carry links and NO self-awarded score, and PRODUCT_EVAL.md states that distinction plainly at the top (FR-063, SC-013). A script that awards itself points for aesthetics is worth nothing to a reader.

area.description: One of the scored areas. Areas and points come straight from the assignment's table so the totals add up and a reader can see which check earns which points.

kind.description: `automated`: eval.py asserts it and reports pass/fail. `evidence`: human judgement — emits links, leaves the score blank.

assertion.description: What must be true. For `evidence` rows, what a reader is being asked to judge.

evidence.description: The query or artifact that shows it — an action row, a probe result, an order id, a cost figure, a live URL.

then.description: Judged rows must not carry a score field. Enforced structurally so self-scoring is not possible by omission.
